turns.message: Imagine I am playing casually and want the game to look as visually detailed and polished as possible, including richer lighting effects. I am willing to sacrifice some FPS for better image quality. Keep my personal controls, crosshair, audio settings, resolution and aspect ratio unchanged.
turns.reply: To achieve a more polished and visually detailed look, I recommend increasing your texture, detail, and UI qualities to High. I also suggest enabling anti-aliasing and anisotropic filtering to smooth out jagged edges and keep textures sharp at steep angles.

recommendations.whyForGoal: Higher texture quality may keep surfaces sharper for a more polished look.
recommendations.tradeoff: Lower settings make surfaces blurrier; Riot advises lowering gradually and testing.

recommendations.tradeoff: Lower settings remove some environmental detail; Riot advises lowering gradually and testing.

recommendations.tradeoff: Lower settings can make interface elements look less crisp.

recommendations.whyForGoal: More anti-aliasing may smooth out jagged edges for a cleaner image.
recommendations.tradeoff: Lower anti-aliasing shows more jagged edges.

recommendations.whyForGoal: Higher anisotropic filtering may keep floor and wall textures sharper at steep angles.
recommendations.tradeoff: Lower filtering makes distant floors and walls blurrier. Higher filtering can cost GPU time, depending on the scene and hardware.

turns.message: Imagine I am playing competitively and want the highest practical frame rate and responsive gameplay while keeping enemies clearly visible. Configure the graphics and frame-pacing settings accordingly, but keep my personal controls, crosshair, audio settings, resolution and aspect ratio unchanged.
turns.reply: To prioritize high frame rates and responsiveness while maintaining clear visibility, I recommend enabling NVIDIA Reflex and disabling V-Sync to reduce input latency. I also suggest lowering several high-impact visual effects like Ambient Occlusion and Parallax Occlusion Mapping to free up GPU resources for a smoother experience.

recommendations.whyForGoal: Enabling NVIDIA Reflex may reduce system latency and increase PC responsiveness for competitive play.
recommendations.tradeoff: Boost may draw more GPU power and slightly reduce FPS (per Valve's tooltip).

recommendations.whyForGoal: Disabling V-Sync may reduce input delay, which is critical for responsive gameplay.
recommendations.tradeoff: Disabling it can reintroduce screen tearing. Synchronising to the display can add input delay on some systems; the size of the effect depends on hardware.

recommendations.whyForGoal: Reducing MSAA may improve your frame rate while still providing some edge smoothing for visibility.
recommendations.tradeoff: Higher sample counts cost more GPU time; lower settings show more jagged edges.

recommendations.whyForGoal: Lowering particle detail may improve performance during effect-heavy moments.
recommendations.tradeoff: Higher detail can degrade performance, especially in effect-heavy moments (Valve).

recommendations.whyForGoal: Disabling Ambient Occlusion may improve your frame rate by reducing lighting calculations.
recommendations.tradeoff: Adds contact shading but can degrade performance (Valve).

recommendations.whyForGoal: Disabling Parallax Occlusion Mapping may improve performance by simplifying surface depth rendering.
recommendations.tradeoff: Adds surface depth but can degrade performance (Valve).

recommendations.whyForGoal: Choosing Performance mode may increase your frame rate and reduce GPU memory usage.
recommendations.tradeoff: Performance mode lowers HDR quality but may increase performance and reduce GPU memory use (Valve).

recommendations.whyForGoal: Reducing shadow quality to Medium may improve frame rate while maintaining enough shadow detail for visibility.
recommendations.tradeoff: Higher shadow quality generally costs more GPU time; the exact effect is hardware dependent.

turns.reply: Ambient occlusion is a rendering technique that calculates how exposed each point in a scene is to ambient lighting. It creates soft shadows in crevices, corners, and where objects meet, which helps define the depth and shape of the environment. In Counter-Strike 2, enabling this can make the world look more realistic but may decrease your frame rate.

turns.message: What is the difference between FPS and monitor refresh rate?
turns.reply: FPS counts how many frames the game renders per second. Refresh rate, in hertz, counts how many times the display can update per second. A 240 Hz monitor can refresh 240 times per second. The frame rate the game produces still depends on the scene, hardware and settings.
